summary:
NOTES: TWO BOOKS (keep separate)

## BOOK 1: The Movie Boys in Peril (Victor Appleton; Garden City 1926)

Chars: Joe Duncan, Blake Stewart (moving-picture boys, chums, own motorcycle, ~90 mph). Mr. Calvert Hadley (Film Theatrical Co. head). Mr. Ringold (dramatic side). C.C. Piper ("Gloomy", grouch). Birdie Lee (Blake's interest). Mabel Pierce (Joe's interest, new member). Nettie Shay (actress). Henry Robertson. Hiram Baker (farm landlord, Central Falls). Mrs. Baker. Hank Duryee (Central Falls livery driver). Rex (spitfire horse, dies in ravine). Vigues Alcando (Spaniard, Equatorial Railroad Co., South America; accent; "Americanized" name). Sam (red-haired barefoot farm boy). Sim Rolinson (postmaster). Capt. Watson (tug Nama). Capt. Wiltsey (tug Bohio). Ramo (educated Indian guide). Capt. Martail (Brazilian steamer captain, Alcando's "distant relative"). Gen. Goethals (chief engineer). Captain/Colonel etc. minor.

Ch I: Boys return on motorcycle to Baker farm near Central Falls, on vacation. No mail from Hadley. Rex bolts with Hank and Alcando; rein breaks; heading for broken bridge (ravine 100 ft; temporary span; sharp curve).
Ch II: Series recap: earlier books (On Call, Wild West, Jungle, Earthquake Land, Mississippi Flood). Boys pursue; cut across field; motorcycle gasoline pipe breaks; Rex crashes fence; carriage hangs on king beam.
Ch III: Boys haul carriage back. Alcando faints briefly (head cut). Card: "Vigues Alcando". Letter from Hadley to boys falls from his pocket.
Ch IV: Alcando says he wants to learn moving pictures; Hadley's letter mentions "when you go to Panama." Alcando's story: company wants jungle railroad films. Boys surprised; no Panama plans.
Ch V: Sam brings delayed special delivery letter (father forgot it in coat). Hadley letter (quoted): Culebra Cut slide expected; small slides followed by big one; Alcando "Johnnie on the Spot"; films for Canal opening.
Ch VI: Boys suspicious of Alcando (resents being saved). Blake reads "History of the Panama Canal" at library. Culebra facts: 9 mi long, avg 120 ft deep, sides 500 ft, bottom 300 ft wide; ditch first 800 ft, later 1800 ft. Decide to go. Blake overhears/sees paper: "go to Panama, get all the pictures you can, especially the big guns." Alcando hides small box.
Ch VII: Alcando: "guns/ones" blunder explanation. Boys to New York. Piper: "buried alive under one of the big Culebra slides."
Ch VIII: Hadley: sail to Colon, HQ Washington Hotel, letters, government permits. Alcando's NY hotel room: cigar smell, hidden visitor, hidden box. Sail on steamer Gatun; Birdie and Mabel wave; Piper: "look out for the big slides."
Ch IX: Alcando buys camping gear (refused). Ticking in his berth: brass-bound box with metal projections. Stop at San Juan, Porto Rico.
Ch X: Alcando angry; calls box "new alarm clock" (his invention); locks in trunk. Colon; Washington Hotel. Balcony talk heard: "Are you sure the machine works right?" "Perfectly."
Ch XI: Tug Nama, Capt. Watson. Runner's message: "You will not fail us?" / "I will not fail--if I have to sacrifice myself." Canal lock explanation (85 ft). Toro Point breakwater (11,000 ft).
Ch XII: Central pier; steel chain fender (3-in links, 100 tons to yield). Gatun lock: Nama pulled backward toward closing gates when towing locomotives fail; stopped just in time. Engineer explains signals.
Ch XIII: 46 gates total; leaves 65 ft wide, 7 ft thick, 300-600 tons; 70 floor openings per lock. Rise 2 ft/min (3 max). Pedro Miguel 30⅓ ft; Miraflores 54⅔ ft. Gatun Dam: 1.5 mi long, 105 ft high; concrete = 3 trips around earth. Dam vulnerable only to dynamite. Boys go to Gamboa and Chagres River.
Ch XIV: Launch; Ramo; leaf-cutting ants; tapirs; orchids ("Holy Ghost"); iguanas (legs tied, tails cut); fruits mamaei, sapodilla. Blake cramp + alligator in river; Joe swims out; Ramo shoots gator (smokeless powder, mushrooming bullet). Alcando: "I wish I had been the one to shoot it."
Ch XV: Week in jungle; back to Gamboa; Culebra Cut. Alcando mutters: "Yes, dynamite here, or at the dam, would do the work."
Ch XVI: Alcando claims "abstract". Capt Watson: "Dynamite! Huh!" Culebra two weeks. Hadley letter: "Don't forget to film the slide." Brazilian steamer crashes Nama at Miraflores pier; Alcando waves to steamer's deck (captain Martail).
Ch XVII: Nama sinks (later raised/wrecked). Boys move to Bohio (Capt. Wiltsey). Alcando asks about double exposure. Blake: "I think he is suspicious of us." Upper lock gate opens by misplaced switch; flood; steel emergency dam swung into place (2 min electric).
Ch XVIII: Boys film flood with two cameras. Alcando helps, "very brave." Hint: Alcando asks "Even if you have to make the slide yourself?" Blake: "Not much!" Big slide at Culebra; Joe and Blake head out.
Ch XIX: Heavy rain; Joe alone with little camera on slope; Blake and Alcando nearby; Joe buried when ground collapses.
Ch XX: Alcando & Blake dig in wrong spot; Indian worker runs for help. Second slide uncovers Joe (rubber coat wrapped around face, camera with him; cut on forehead, unconscious then revived). Joe taken to Bohio; doctor at Gatun.
Ch XXI: Blake spends week at Culebra; Gen. Goethals orders work. Joe recovers at Gatun. Joe reports Alcando muttering: "I just hate to do it, though I'll have to, I suppose. But I'll not put the blame on--". Blake thinks Alcando a poor operator. Alcando goes off with small camera; ticking heard from film case.
Ch XXII: Alcando: "alarm clock," can't perfect one feature. Blake reads fragment: "Stuff is all ready for you. You had better do the job and get away. There is some fine scenery in Europe." Alcando says he left camera and clock at dam. Capt. Wiltsey: rumor dam to be dynamited tonight; boys asked to film with flashlights.
Ch XXIII: Plan: magnesium flash, automatic camera (clockwork, trigger string, continuous flash), high-voltage battery. Rumors from disaffected foreign laborers; South Americans distrusted.
Ch XXIV: Boys set cameras near spillway. Joe fixes wire. Ticking heard in dark ("tick-tick-tick").
Ch XXV: Blake and Joe search by sound; magnesium flash; Alcando seen advancing toward dam, caught by soldiers. Blake cuts wires with pliers. Small dynamite charge found (not enough to do much damage).
Ch XXV cont.: Alcando confesses: Brazilian railroad plot (stockholder behind it; railroad profits threatened by Canal) to scare shippers, not destroy dam; planned to frame camera boys; he was threatened; sacrifice of himself. Escapes from prison that night.
Ch XXVI: Plotters vanished; seen later in European capital. Railroad disowns plot. Stricter rules for Canal visitors. Brass box = timer. Canal opens; boys take pleasure trip. Next book: "The Movie Boys Under the Sea." Blake gets letter, plans to return to New York.

## BOOK 2: The Pomp of Yesterday (Joseph Hocking; Hodder & Stoughton)

Front matter: epigraph Kipling "Recessional" ("Lest we forget"). Foreword: asks "Why is Victory delayed?"; Somme descriptions from witnesses; author visited front twice; finished August 1917; Russia anticipated. Dedication: Gen. Sir William Robertson, March 2, 1918 ("Let us never forget... faith of our forefathers").

Narrator: Captain Luscombe (Cornishman; recruiting officer; "Major" later). Other key chars: Paul Edgecumbe (amnesiac; later Jack Carbis, son of Lord & Lady Carbis, Lord Carbis = brewer, peer created 1890). Sir Roger Granville (Granitelands, Devon). Colonel Gray. Norah Blackwater (tall, ~25, engaged to George). George St. Mabyn (~28, Territorial captain, wounded Ypres; later Major). Maurice St. Mabyn (elder brother, reported killed in Egypt April 1914; actually alive). Captain Horace Springfield (~30-35; tall, dark, lean; scar on cheek under right temple; receding forehead; villain). Lorna Bolivick (19-20; childlike, brown eyes; father Sir Thomas Bolivick; mother Lady Bolivick; estate Bolivick near South Petherwin; brothers Tom and another at front). Charlie Buller (~24, Devonshire yeomanry, lieutenant, wounded; suitor). Dr. Merril (South Petherwin). Colonel McClure (Plymouth St George's Military Hospital; 12 yrs India). Colonel Heywood (artillery; OTC). Sergeant Smith. Jenkins (orderly). Corporal Wilkins. Captain Wilkins (in one message).

Ch I: Plymouth Harbour, early spring 1915. Man with ageless face, no memory, from Bombay (after India; scars, Indians torture memory). Named Paul Edgecumbe (Mount Edgecumbe; Paul from scripture). Luscombe dines him; recruits him. Edgecumbe speaks at Plymouth meeting, volunteers: "Will you take me, sir?" "how can a man, who is a man, do anything else?" Disappears afterward.
Ch II: Luscombe sent to Falmouth; Sir Roger reminisces about Edgecumbe. Granitelands visit; Lady Granville; three ladies.
Ch III: Norah Blackwater (engaged to Maurice; now to George). Lorna: "Mr. Luscombe was meant to meet him." Luscombe promises Lorna to find Edgecumbe and write her; diary May 29 witnessed by Lorna. St. Mabyn's haunted look.
Ch IV: St. Pinto? Actually St. Mabyn's house in Devon; Springfield introduced; claims Maurice killed in Egypt by mullah's rebels; Springfield present ("pal"). Lorna's second request: tell her when found. Springfield "snakes" (Norah). Luscombe captured in No Man's Land raid.
Ch V: Luscombe in German dug-out with Sergeant Smith; British shelling; Edgecumbe (in Tommy's uniform) persuades ~30 Germans to surrender, "miracle."
Ch VI: Edgecumbe recognized; decorated; Luscombe asks about memory; Luscombe says Edgecumbe "unmasks" Springfield description; Edgecumbe reacts with contempt. Colonel reports Edgecumbe missing.
Ch VII: Edgecumbe returns wounded; speech on drink (firemen in pubs delayed troop ship 24 hrs; munitions delays; Lloyd George quote "put down the drink"). St. Mabyn enters; sees Edgecumbe, relieved.
Ch VIII: St. Mabyn says he and Norah engaged. Lorna's Y.M.C.A. / nursing; luscombe eavesdrops in copse: Springfield and St. Mabyn plot, "if it is he, he must never go back to England alive." Springfield: "Foul play, my son?"
Ch IX: Springfield dines; Edgecumbe missing after shot. Found? No; reported missing.
Ch X: Lorna's letter (wants photograph, "I command you"). Somme 1 July 1916 described; Luscombe captured again by three Germans; Edgecumbe rescues him ("twice you've saved my life").
Ch XI: Edgecumbe's story: poisoned at quarry earlier; Y.M.C.A. hut, converted to Christianity (New Testament). Hears Springfield's Indian cry (vendetta); recognizes him. Lorna's letter praises Edgecumbe's photo.
Ch XII: Somme advance; Springfield buried; Edgecumbe digs him out. Luscombe shell-shocked; Colonel Gray. Edgecumbe in boat to England; "I have become a Christian."
Ch XIII: Edgecumbe's teaching: war must be fought in God's strength; drink; Admiral Beatty and Sir W. Robertson quotes; Victor Hugo on Waterloo; Germany "fighting devil's battle."
Ch XIV: Edgecumbe's logic on drink & impurity; Lorna invites them to Bolivick.
Ch XV: Colonel Heywood: Edgecumbe is an artillery genius; Devonshire journey; Bolivick (Lorna waiting; Edgecumbe stares).
Ch XVI: Dinner; Edgecumbe says he dreamt of her; Luscombe tells story of 30 prisoners; Sir Thomas delighted. Buller and Springfield arrive.
Ch XVII: Springfield's "Charlie Buller"; Springfield thanks Edgecumbe for saving his life, hatred visible; Edgecumbe says "I know him." Edgecumbe confesses love for Lorna.
Ch XVIII: Edgecumbe: "I love her," "there's that man." Lorna's walk. Edgecumbe collapses before dinner.
Ch XIX: Dr. Merril: suspects poison. Luscombe drives to Plymouth with Buller; Springfield offers to go instead; Luscombe refuses.
Ch XX: Colonel McClure at night; drives back; Sir Thomas says doctors "It's all over."
Ch XXI: Edgecumbe's hands; blue spot on lower left arm (injected poison); McClure's Indian antidote; Edgecumbe recovers. Luscombe's suspicions discussed (poisoning, Springfield).
Ch XXII: Edgecumbe wants Lorna; Luscombe warns (no name, no money, possible wife). Springfield at lunch flirting with Lorna.
Ch XXIII: Luscombe questions Springfield about poison (Springfield denies). Sir Thomas: Springfield to inherit Carbis peerage; brewer peer. McClure: "watch over him."
Ch XXIV: Edgecumbe proposes to Lorna in woods; she refuses ("I don't love you... never can"). Edgecumbe bravely suppresses; dinner gaiety; Sir Thomas: "genius." London trip next.
Ch XXV: Train from Bristol; "Why is Victory delayed?" Edgecumbe on Kipling, drink, God; "Where does God come in?"
Ch XXVI: Paddington: Springfield seen; Luscombe warns Edgecumbe. Edgecumbe at Y.M.C.A. hostel, then Luscombe's hotel. House of Commons; Minister (Luscombe's friend); Edgecumbe's questions on God.
Ch XXVII: Waterloo station troops; vice; revue music-hall; tea room; London night walk.
Ch XXVIII: Churches; hospital for venereal disease; Crystal Palace sailors; Lorna at restaurant with Springfield (Sir Thomas, Lady B there). Edgecumbe: "To save a woman's soul."
Ch XXIX: Springfield now Colonel; Lorna and Springfield; Springfield attacks Edgecumbe; Edgecumbe on drink, Hadley-like; Edgecumbe ordered to front; Luscombe on sick leave.
Ch XXX: Narrative in 1917. Edgecumbe letters: captaincy; Somme halted; German submarine threat; food shortage; Russian Revolution; US declares war; Wilson speech; Kaiser prophecy.
Ch XXXI: June 1917: Edgecumbe returns (left arm sling). Springfield framed him (claimed German officer in Berlin); Edgecumbe exonerated; DSO. Times article praising him. Telegram from Bolivick.
Ch XXXII: London meeting: Edgecumbe speaks; drink/impurity; General says "worth more than an army corps."
Ch XXXIII: Bolivick; Lord & Lady Carbis arrive; Lady Carbis: "Jack! our Jack!"; Edgecumbe collapses.
Ch XXXIV: Memory restored ("the black curtain" lifted). Dinner; Lorna's engagement to Springfield talk.
Ch XXXV: Carbis family; Jack confirms; Dr. Merril checks.
Ch XXXVI: Jack refuses to benefit from drink money. Lorna says she'll marry Springfield (later reveals blackmail). Jack's stance.
Ch XXXVII: Jack tells Maurice's story: Springfield stabbed Maurice in Egypt; Maurice later reported to General Gregory (died 2 yrs ago).
Ch XXXVIII: Jack confronts Springfield at dinner; reveals Maurice alive July 1914 (Bizna, India); Springfield proposes to Lorna; denies everything.
Ch XXXIX: Maurice St. Mabyn appears; Springfield exposed; leaves; Lorna looks at him.
Ch XL: Maurice's generosity; George's guilt; Maurice refuses to forgive Norah. Springfield found dead in Plymouth hotel (Indian poison); sealed package not to be opened within a week of burial.
Ch XLI: Springfield's letter ("Life's not worth living"). Jack and Luscombe; Jack's views now (England spiritually changed; God's time). Jack returns to front in 4 days.
Ch XLII: Lorna at Bolivick; Luscombe reveals Springfield's blackmail (Jack's Indian crimes threat); Lorna admits love. Jack follows Luscombe; Lorna and Jack walk; engagement; Luscombe as brother; Jack goes to see Sir Thomas. (Story unfinished.)
